attributes.proposal_description: Giiyo Tech proposes a 3-month blockchain training program to equip 50 participants in Cameroon with hands-on skills in blockchain development, governance, and ecosystem participation. The program includes instructor-led sessions, access to necessary infrastructure (computers, internet, power backup), and CBCA certification upon completion. The training will be conducted by experienced blockchain professionals and will cover smart contracts, dApps, and governance participation within the Cardano ecosystem.
attributes.key_proposal_deliverables:
-50 participants successfully trained and certified.
-50 computers set up with necessary blockchain development tools.
-Starlink internet installed and operational.
-Participants actively engaging in Cardano’s governance and ecosystem post-training.
attributes.resourcing_duration_estimates:
Resourcing & Duration Estimates:
Team: 3 instructors, 2 administrative staff, and 1 program coordinator.
Duration: 3 months of training + 1 month for preparation.

attributes.problem_statement:
Cardano’s mission to bank the unbanked in Africa is ambitious, but in Cameroon, it is running into real-world roadblocks. The country has brilliant tech minds, but they are underrepresented in the Cardano ecosystem. This is not due to lack of interest but because of the following challenges. 
-Limited Access to Structured Education: There are no structured training programs tailored to Cardano. If you want to learn, collaborate, or get into governance offline, you are basically on your own.          
-Cardano Ignores Local realities.  Most tools are built without African use 
cases in mind. e.g most wallets don’t have Mobile money wallet payment or they don’t work. Also, developer tools assume constant internet and electricity, locking out builders in offline-heavy markets like Cameroon. Only about 60% of Cameroonians have internet access, and even then, connections are slow and unreliable. Frequent power cuts make it difficult for developers to work consistently.
-Governance Participation Deficit. Limited understanding of protocol parameters, CIPs, or DRep roles in emerging communities.

Without intervention, Cameroonians risk being left behind while the rest of the world builds the future of finance.
attributes.proposal_benefit:
The Cardano Builders Community Bootcamp is a three-month intensive program designed to equip Cameroonian developers with the skills, infrastructure, and knowledge necessary to build impactful decentralized applications (dApps) on the Cardano blockchain. By implementing this training program, we will:
-Equip 50 participants with blockchain development skills, increasing the talent pool for Cardano-related projects.
-Provide hands-on training, mentorship, and certification, ensuring participants are ready to contribute to the ecosystem.
-Foster local blockchain adoption, strengthening the Cardano community in Africa.
-Create a model that can be replicated in other regions to drive global adoption.
